\boxed{N}

The $N$-th rational solution is a quotient of double-Wronskians of size $N$; its poles in $x$ are the zeros of the denominator $D_N(x,t)$.  
$D_N$ is a real polynomial in $x$ of degree $2N$, so non-real zeros occur in complex-conjugate pairs.  
For large $|t|$, the asymptotic behaviour in each of the $N$ soliton frames is controlled by a leading-order polynomial of degree $N$. By hypothesis this polynomial has exactly $N$ real roots.  
Each such real root perturbs to a simple conjugate pair of zeros of $D_N$, one in $\operatorname{Im}x>0$ and one in $\operatorname{Im}x<0$.  
Rouché’s theorem excludes any further zeros in the upper half-plane.  
Therefore the $N$-th solution admits exactly $N$ poles in the upper half-plane of $x$ for large $|t|$.

The $N$-th double-Wronskian rational solution is generated by a Jordan chain of length $N$ at the embedded eigenvalue, so its dominant (large-$|t|$) denominator polynomial is of degree $N$ in $x$.  
The $N$ real roots of this leading-order polynomial give the asymptotic velocities of the $N$ constituent algebraic solitons.  
Each algebraic soliton contributes exactly one simple pole in $\operatorname{Im}x>0$ (with a conjugate pole in $\operatorname{Im}x<0$).  
Because all $N$ leading roots are real, all $N$ poles remain in (or approach from) the upper half-plane for large $|t|$, with none migrating to the lower half-plane.  
Hence the number of poles in the upper half-plane is $N$.

\boxed{N}

For large $|t|$ the $N$-th double-Wronskian rational solution asymptotically separates into $N$ well-separated fundamental algebraic solitons. Each algebraic soliton contributes exactly one simple pole in $\operatorname{Im}x>0$, located at the real root of its associated leading-order polynomial shifted by a fixed positive imaginary amount (determined by the common mass). The assumption that the leading-order polynomials possess exactly $N$ real roots guarantees that no additional complex roots—and hence no extra upper-half-plane poles—appear. Therefore the total number of poles in the upper half-plane of $x$ is $N$.

The $N$-th rational solution is generated by an embedded eigenvalue of algebraic multiplicity $N$, so for large $|t|$ it asymptotically separates into $N$ distinct algebraic solitons of identical mass. In each soliton region the double-Wronskian denominator factorizes, to leading order, into a polynomial whose real zero determines the soliton center; the hypothesis that these leading-order polynomials possess exactly $N$ real roots guarantees $N$ distinct centers with no collisions on the real axis. Each algebraic soliton contributes exactly one simple pole in the upper half-plane of $x$ (its conjugate lying in the lower half-plane), and no additional poles survive in the asymptotic regime. Hence the total number of upper-half-plane poles is $N$.
